301: Holding back anger only counts when you could actually hurt someone with it. If your anger has no power to do harm anyway, what does it matter whether you hold it back or not?
302: Getting angry at people stronger than you only hurts you. Getting angry at people weaker than you, who cannot fight back, is the worst evil of all.
303: Let go of your anger at anyone at all, and forget it, because every kind of harm grows out of anger.
304: Anger kills the smile on your face and the joy in your heart. Is there any enemy worse than that?
305: If you want to protect yourself, keep your anger in check. If you don’t, your own anger will destroy you.
306: Anger is a fire that kills anyone who comes near it. It even burns up your family and friends, who are like a raft that carries you safely through life.
307: A person who treats anger as something precious will surely be ruined, just as someone who hits the ground with their hand will surely hurt that hand.
308: Even if someone hurts you as badly as throwing you into a blazing fire, it is good, if you possibly can, not to get angry with them.
309: If a person never lets even a thought of anger into their mind, they will right away get everything they hope for.
310: People who let their anger go beyond all limits are as good as dead. People who have given up anger completely are as great as holy people who have left the world behind.
311: Even if hurting someone would bring them great riches and fame, people with pure minds keep firmly to their rule of never causing pain to others.
312: Even when someone hurts them out of hate, people with pure minds make it their rule not to hurt that person back.
313: Even if people hate and hurt you when you did nothing to them, hurting them back will later bring you sorrow you cannot escape.
314: The best way to punish people who hurt you is to be so kind to them that they feel ashamed, and then to let the matter go.
315: What good is all your learning if you do not feel another creature’s pain as your own and protect it from suffering?
316: Whatever you have learned is painful from your own experience, never do that to anyone else.
317: The highest goodness is never to do anything low or hurtful to anyone, however small, at any time, not even in your thoughts.
318: A person knows well how pain feels in their own life. So why do they cause that same pain to other living beings?
319: If you harm others in the morning, harm will come back to you on its own by the afternoon.
320: All suffering comes back to those who cause suffering. So people who want to be free of suffering do not cause it to others.
321: If you ask what doing good means, it is not killing any living thing. Killing brings every other kind of evil deed along with it.
322: Sharing your food with others and protecting all kinds of living things is the greatest of all the good deeds that wise writers have listed in their books.
323: Not killing stands alone as the greatest good. Right behind it, in second place, comes not lying.
324: If you ask what the good path is, it is the way of life that takes care never to kill any creature at all.
325: Many people give up the world because they fear the endless cycle of life and death. The greatest of them is the one who fears the wrong of killing and carefully keeps from it.
326: Death, which eats up all lives, will not come to cut short the days of someone who has made not killing the rule they live by.
327: Even if it costs you your own life, do not do anything that takes away the precious life of another being.
328: Even if people say the gain from killing is great and good, good-hearted people see any gain that comes from killing as the lowest of things.
329: People who kill for a living are seen as doers of shameful deeds by those who understand what truly low behavior is.
330: Wise people say that those who now live poor, miserable lives in sick bodies are the ones who once took the lives of other beings.
331: Believing that things which cannot last will last forever is the worst kind of foolishness.
332: Great riches come together like a crowd gathering to watch a show, and they leave like that crowd going home when the show is over.
333: Riches never stay for long. So when you have them, use them right away to do good deeds that will last.
334: A day looks like just a stretch of time. But people who understand know it is really a saw, cutting away at your life bit by bit.
335: Before your tongue stops working and the death rattle (the last breathing sound of a dying person) rises in your throat, hurry to do good deeds.
336: This world has a strange kind of greatness: someone who was here yesterday is gone today.
337: People cannot know if they will live even one more moment, yet they make countless plans, more than ten million of them.
338: The friendship between the body and the soul is like a bird that flies away and leaves its egg (or nest) behind, empty and alone.
339: Death is like falling asleep, and being born is like waking up after sleep.
340: The soul only stays for a while in a corner of the body. It seems it has not yet found a lasting home of its own.
341: Whatever a person has let go of, whatever it may be, that thing can no longer cause them pain.
342: If you want lasting good, give things up while you still have them. Once you have given them up, many joys come to you even in this life.
343: You must control your five senses and, at the same time, give up all the things they crave.
344: Owning nothing at all is natural for someone who has truly given up the world. Owning even one thing pulls them back into the false thinking they had left behind.
345: For people working to end the cycle of being born again and again, even their own body is one thing too many. So why take on any more ties?
346: A person who cuts away the pride of thinking “I” and “mine” will reach a world higher even than the world of the gods.
347: Sorrows grab hold and never let go of people who hold tightly to the things they are attached to and will not let them go.
348: People who have given up everything completely have reached the highest goal. All others are confused and caught in a net.
349: The moment a person lets go of all attachments, the cycle of rebirth is cut. Otherwise, they keep going round and round in an endless, unsteady cycle of birth and death.
350: Hold on to the One who is free of all attachment. Hold on to that one bond alone, so that you can let go of all others.
351: Thinking that things which are not real are the real thing is a mistake of the mind. From this mistake come lowly births, again and again.
352: People who have left confusion behind and see the truth clearly and without fault find that this clear sight drives away darkness and brings true joy.
353: For people who have moved past doubt and become truly certain, heaven is closer than the earth they stand on.
354: Even if someone has fully learned everything the five senses can tell them, it is of no real use if they do not truly know what is real.
355: Whatever a thing is, and however it looks, wisdom is seeing the real truth inside it.
356: People who have learned and have seen the True Reality here in this life set off on the path of no return, never to be born into this world again.
357: If the mind has carefully studied and firmly understood what is truly real, there is no need to think about being born again.
358: True wisdom is seeing the perfect Truth, the Highest Good, so that the foolishness called “birth” is taken away.
359: Whoever understands the true Support that holds up all things, and lives so that all lesser attachments fall away, will be free of the sorrows that would otherwise cling to them and ruin their efforts.
360: When desire, anger and confusion are destroyed so completely that even their names are gone, the suffering they cause is destroyed too.
361: Wise people say that desire is the seed that, for every living being and at all times, never fails to cause one birth after another.
362: If you must want something, want to be free from being born again. That freedom comes only when you want to be free of wanting.
363: There is no treasure in this world as precious as being free from desire. Even in the next world, nothing is equal to it.
364: Being pure means nothing other than being free from desire, and that freedom comes from longing for the truth.
365: Only people who have cut off desire truly deserve to be called people who have given up the world. Others, whatever they have given up, are not fully free like them.
366: Being on guard against desire is itself goodness, because it is desire that fools a person and ruins them.
367: If a person cuts off desire completely, the good deeds that lead to a life free from death will come to them just as they wish.
368: People without desire have no sorrow. Wherever desire exists, sorrow keeps coming, one after another, without fail.
369: When desire, the worst of all sorrows, is destroyed, joy flows without stopping, even in this life.
370: Desire by its nature can never be satisfied. Whoever throws it away gains, at that very moment, a lasting happiness that never changes.
371: When fate is ready to bring you riches, it makes you work hard without tiring. When fate is ready to take riches away, it makes you lazy.
372: When fate brings loss, it makes even a clever person act foolishly. When fate brings gain, it opens up a person’s mind and makes it wider.
373: However many deep books a person studies, in the end the understanding that fate has given them is what wins out.
374: Fate works in two different ways in the world. Becoming rich is one thing, and becoming wise is quite another.
375: When you are trying to get rich, fate can turn every good chance into a bad one, and every bad chance into a good one.
376: What fate has not made yours will not stay, however carefully you guard it. What fate has made yours will not leave, even if you throw it away.
377: Even people who pile up crores (tens of millions) of money can enjoy it only as much as the One who decides fate allows. Beyond that, they cannot enjoy it.
378: Poor people, who have nothing to enjoy, would give up the world, if only fate let the sufferings meant for them pass by without making them go through them.
379: People who happily accept good times as good, why should they get upset when bad times come? Both come from the same fate.
380: What is stronger than fate? Even when a person finds another way to escape it, fate gets there first.
381: A ruler who has all six parts of a strong country (an army, loyal people, riches, wise advisers, friendly allies and strong forts) is like a lion among kings.
382: Courage, generosity, wisdom and energy: never lacking these four is the true nature of a king.
383: Being alert and never slow, being learned, and being brave and firm: these three must never leave those who rule a land.
384: A true king never turns away from what is right, removes what is wrong from the land, and keeps a brave sense of honor that never falls short.
385: A good ruler knows how to create sources of money, collect it, keep it safe, and then share out what was kept safe in a wise way.
386: If a king is easy for his people to meet and never speaks harshly, the whole world will praise his land.
387: For a ruler who gives with kind words and protects the people, the world will praise him and follow his word, just as he wishes.
388: A king who rules fairly and protects his people will be seen by them as a god.
389: The whole world will live safely under the royal umbrella (the sign of his rule) of a king who is kind enough to listen to words that are bitter to hear.
390: A king who has these four things, generosity, kindness, fair rule and care for his people, is the light among kings.
391: Learn what is worth learning, and learn it fully, without gaps. Then live in a way that matches what you have learned.
392: What we call numbers and what we call letters, wise people say, are the two eyes of every living person.
393: Only educated people can truly be said to have eyes. People without learning just have two sores on their face.
394: This is the sign of learned people: others are happy to meet them, and when they leave, others keep thinking of them and want to meet them again.
395: People who stand respectfully before their teachers, as eager as the poor before the rich, and so gain learning, are truly great. Those who will not do this to learn are the lowest of all.
396: A well dug in sand gives more water the deeper it is dug. In the same way, a person’s understanding grows the more they learn.
397: For a learned person, every country and every town becomes their own. So why does anyone stay without learning right up to the day they die?
398: The learning a person gains in one life can protect and help them for seven lives to come.
399: When learned people see that the learning that brings them joy also brings joy to the whole world, they love learning even more.
400: Learning is the one great treasure that can never be destroyed. Compared with it, all the other things people own are not real treasure at all.
401: Speaking in a gathering of learned people without having fully learned your subject is like playing dice without a game board.
402: An uneducated person who wants to be admired as a speaker is like a woman with no breasts wishing to be desired as a woman.
403: Even uneducated people will be thought of as very good, as long as they stay quiet in front of learned people.
404: Even if an uneducated person’s cleverness happens to be very good, wise people will not accept it as reliable.
405: An uneducated person’s high opinion of themselves fades away as soon as they meet and talk with learned people.
406: Uneducated people can only be said to exist. Beyond that, they are like salty land where nothing grows.
407: The good looks of a person who lacks deep, sharp understanding are like the beauty of a painted clay doll.
408: Riches in the hands of uneducated people cause more misery than being poor causes for good people.
409: Even if they are born into a high family, uneducated people are not worth as much as learned people born into a low one.
410: Uneducated people compare to those who have studied great books the way animals compare to human beings.
411: The riches you gain through your ears, by listening to wise people, are the treasure of all treasures. Of all riches, they come first.
412: Only when there is nothing to feed the ears, no good teaching to listen to, should you give a little food to the stomach as well.
413: People who have gained knowledge by listening, which is food for the ears, are equal on earth to the gods, who are fed by offerings in sacred fires.
414: Even if you have not studied, listen to learned people. What you hear will hold you up like a walking stick when you are weak or in trouble.
415: The words of good people are like a walking stick for someone walking on slippery ground.
416: Listen to good things, even if only a little. Even that little will bring you great honor.
417: People who have studied things closely and gathered much learning by listening will not say foolish things, even when they have understood something wrongly.
418: Ears that have not been pierced (opened up) by good teaching are no better than deaf ears, even though they hear sounds.
419: People who have not gained fine, deep learning by listening find it hard to speak gently and politely.
420: Some people know only the tastes of the mouth and not the tastes of the ear, like animals. What does it matter whether they live or die?
421: Wisdom is a weapon that protects a person from ruin. It is also a fort inside them that enemies cannot break into or destroy.
422: Wisdom means not letting the mind run wherever it wants. It keeps the mind away from evil and guides it toward good.
423: Whatever you hear, and whoever you hear it from, wisdom is finding the real truth of it.
424: Wisdom is speaking so that others easily understand you and remember what you said, and also catching the deeper meaning in what others say.
425: It is smart to make friends with the good and great people of the world. It is wise to keep that friendship steady, not opening up like a flower at first and closing up later.
426: Wisdom is living in step with the world, behaving the way the best people in the world behave.
427: Wise people know what is going to happen before it happens. Unwise people cannot know it.
428: Not being afraid of what you should be afraid of is foolish. Being afraid of what you should be afraid of is the way of the wise.
429: Wise people who prepare ahead for what is coming will never be hit by a disaster that makes them shake with fear.
430: People who have wisdom have everything. People without wisdom have nothing, whatever else they own.
431: The success of people who are free from pride, anger and low desires has real worth and is respected.
432: Being stingy, having pride about the wrong things, and taking joy in unworthy things are faults that harm a ruler.
433: People who fear shame treat even a fault as small as a millet seed as if it were as big as a palmyra palm (a very tall tree).
434: Make guarding against faults your main goal, because faults are the very enemy that brings ruin.
435: A person who does not guard against faults before they come will see their life destroyed, like a pile of straw in front of a fire.
436: If a ruler first fixes his own faults and only then looks at the faults of others, what fault could ever harm him?
437: The riches of a stingy person who does not use them for what they should be used for will not last. They will be lost without doing any good.
438: Stinginess, the greedy grip that holds on to everything, is not counted along with other faults. It stands apart as worse than all of them.
439: Never, at any time, think too highly of yourself, and never want to do things that bring no good.
440: If you can enjoy what you love without letting others know what you want, your enemies’ plans against you will fail.
441: Learn the right way to do it, think carefully, and then win the friendship of people who know dharma (the right way to live) and have grown wise.
442: Value and make your own the people who can solve troubles that have already come and protect you from troubles that are still to come.
443: Of all rare things, the rarest is to respect great people and make them your own family.
444: Living in such a way that people greater than you become your own is the greatest of all strengths.
445: A king must use his advisers as his eyes, so he should choose them only after thinking very carefully.
446: Enemies can do nothing against someone who is able to live as one of a group of good and worthy people.
447: Who can ruin people who keep friends brave enough to scold them when they are wrong?
448: A king without anyone to scold and correct him has no protection, and he will be ruined even when no enemy is there to destroy him.
449: Just as there is no profit without money to start with, there is no steadiness for those without good people to support them.
450: Losing the friendship of good people is ten times worse than making many enemies.
